predecessors.name: Babylonia
predecessors.text: Babylonia, restored as an independent kingdom by Nabopolassar

predecessors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
predecessors.text: the Assyrian heartland and "the lands west of the Euphrates" and the Levant that Babylon took in the partition

successors.name: Achaemenid Empire
successors.text: the whole Neo-Babylonian territory, conquered by Cyrus in 539

ledger.x: Nov. 626 BC: Nabopolassar is crowned King of Babylon. "In 626 BC, Nabopolassar assaulted and successfully seized the cities of Babylon and Nippur. In November 626 BC, Nabopolassar was crowned King of Babylon." Same state as Babylonia, now the Chaldean dynasty.
620 BC: Nabopolassar controls most of Babylonia.
612 BC: Nineveh falls to the Medes and Babylonians.
c. 553 BC: Nabonidus takes Tayma. He "settled for ten years in the conquered city of Tayma in northern Arabia" and returned c. 543; the year is derived (543 plus ten), the page dates no conquest.
539 BC (bridged): Tyre's tie ends with the empire.

12 Oct. 539 BC: Babylon falls to Cyrus. The Battle of Opis was in 539 BC and Babylon fell "On 12 October" after the Euphrates was diverted; "Babylon never again attained the status of an independent state". Infobox end 539 BC.

wars.name: Nabopolassar's war of independence
wars.outcome: Nabopolassar took Babylon and Nippur (626) and most of Babylonia (620); the Medes and Babylon took Assur (614), Nineveh (612) and Harran (609) and divided the empire.

wars.name: Battle of Carchemish and conquest of Hamath
wars.outcome: Nebuchadnezzar "decisively defeated" Egypt at Carchemish; Necho II's forces "completely annihilated"; "Nebuchadnezzar conquered all of Ha[ma]th".

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar's Philistine and Judean wars
wars.outcome: Ashkelon levelled in 604; Jerusalem taken in 597; destroyed in 587/586 after Zedekiah stopped paying tribute in 589.

wars.name: Siege of Tyre
wars.outcome: Tyre "eventually surrendered to him in 573 BC"; the island city kept its own kings.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar's Egyptian and Arabian campaigns
wars.outcome: "In the 601 BC campaign, Nebuchadnezzar departed from the Levant and then marched into Egypt"; "It is possible that Nebuchadnezzar campaigned against Egypt in 568-567 BC"; the attack was repelled.

wars.name: Cyrus's conquest of Babylon
wars.outcome: The Battle of Opis in 539 and the fall of Babylon on 12 October after the Euphrates was diverted; Nabonidus was the last king.

certainty.note: All frontiers are approximate; the Median Wall "built to defend Babylonia against incursions from the north" (Nebuchadnezzar II page) marks the northern edge of the core but is not dated.
